Victoria Plaisir

October 6, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy / Principles Recovery Center

Dear Hiring Manager:

I am excited to apply for the Outreach Manager – Behavioral Health position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With more than six years of experience supporting youth, families, and community-based programs, I have developed a strong background in community outreach, relationship building, participant engagement, resource navigation, and coordinated service delivery. I am particularly interested in this opportunity because it combines relationship development with helping individuals and families connect to services that can meaningfully improve their lives.

In my current role as a Success Coach with Hispanic Unity of Florida, I manage a caseload of more than 25 youth and families and work directly with participants to identify needs, develop individualized service plans, coordinate referrals, and connect families with appropriate community resources. I regularly collaborate with interdisciplinary teams and community partners to address barriers affecting participant progress. I also coordinate family engagement workshops and support events designed to strengthen participation and community relationships. This experience has strengthened my ability to build trust, communicate effectively with diverse stakeholders, identify needs, and follow through to ensure individuals are connected with the appropriate resources.

Previously, as a Program Specialist with Big Brothers Big Sisters of Miami, I worked extensively with youth, families, volunteers, schools, and community partners. I supported more than 75 youth and volunteer mentoring matches and conducted outreach initiatives focused on recruiting and engaging participants. I also collaborated with schools and community organizations to address barriers affecting student success. Through this work, I developed a strong understanding of how effective outreach depends on consistent relationship management, clear communication, and the ability to understand the needs of both the individuals being served and the organizations serving them.

I also bring strong experience with program documentation, data tracking, and CRM systems. At Big Brothers Big Sisters of Miami, I used Salesforce to document services, track participant outcomes, maintain records, and support reporting. In my current position, I maintain accurate participant documentation and ensure services and referrals are properly coordinated and documented. I understand that successful outreach is not simply about making connections; it also requires organized follow-through, measurable activity, and strong communication with internal teams. These skills would allow me to effectively coordinate with Admissions, maintain outreach activity within a CRM, and support timely connections to care.

My earlier experience at Riverside House further strengthened my ability to work with individuals experiencing complex circumstances. I conducted daily intakes, coordinated services for more than 30 clients, monitored program compliance, maintained confidential records, and responded to crises using de-escalation techniques and established emergency protocols. This experience taught me the importance of professionalism, discretion, empathy, and sound judgment when working with individuals and families who may be navigating significant challenges.

I am especially drawn to the opportunity to represent both Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center within the community. The ability to educate schools, healthcare professionals, therapists, treatment providers, and community organizations about available programs while helping facilitate connections to appropriate care is work I find meaningful. I would bring a relationship-driven, organized, and service-oriented approach to developing referral partnerships and expanding awareness of behavioral health resources throughout the community.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background in youth services, community outreach, participant engagement, resource coordination, and program operations can contribute to the continued growth of Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Sincerely,

Victoria Plaisir

Dear Hiring Manager/Team at Adolescent Wellness Academy,

I am writing to express my strong interest in the Adolescent Services Manager position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a Master’s degree in Human Services and over 28 years of experience leading child welfare teams, I am excited about the opportunity to bring my background in quality assurance and program excellence to your organization.

Throughout my career, I have focused on translating complex state regulations into high-quality, day-to-day care.  As a manager, I have led and mentored teams of 20 to 35 case managers and supervisors. By balancing caseloads, providing targeted staff coaching, and streamlining paperwork, I have successfully maintained high standards of care while keeping staff burnout low.

I also bring a strong background in risk management and compliance.  I have personally led internal audit preparations and file reviews for formal Florida DCF reviews to ensure our daily operations met every state requirement. In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English. As my son, progressed and I was forced to stay home.  I found work on line, which happened to be during COVID.

Dear Hiring Committee,
I am writing to express my interest in the Clinic Director position with the Adolescent Wellness Academy as you expand into North Carolina. With more than 20 years of experience in adolescent behavioral health, residential and PHP/IOP leadership, clinical operations, and program development, I have built a career dedicated to helping teens and families navigate high stress moments with clarity, compassion, and evidence based support. As a licensed Marriage and Family Therapist, the mission and values of AWA align deeply with my own leadership philosophy and the environments I strive to create.
My entrepreneurial background includes creating, launching and scaling inpatient and outpatient programs, overseeing multidisciplinary clinical and operational teams, and building high quality workflows that support strong outcomes and regulatory compliance. I have led admissions processes, treatment planning, crisis response, and discharge coordination while ensuring documentation quality, accreditation readiness, and risk management. 
I am particularly energized by the opportunity to lead AWA’s first North Carolina facility. I have a proven track record of building values driven cultures where staff feel supported, challenged, and connected to a shared mission. My leadership style is collaborative and people first, clear, and accountable, rooted in radical candor, consistent feedback, and a commitment to helping teams grow. communication, and someone willing to help find a solution.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the opportunity to work with adolescents and families. Throughout my career, I have developed extensive experience supporting adolescents who are at risk of requiring placement in alternative settings, as well as youth with intellectual, developmental, and mental health disabilities. My work has centered on helping adolescents recognize their strengths, establish meaningful goals, develop life skills, and build the confidence and skills necessary to function successfully at home, in school, and within their communities.

My experience with adolescents began in an educational after-school setting, where I served as a director of a program for at-risk middle school students. In this role, I provided supervision and individualized support while assisting students with their educational needs, social development, problem-solving, and life skills. I worked to create a structured and supportive environment where adolescents could receive academic assistance while also developing the interpersonal and practical skills needed to be successful outside of the classroom.

I have also worked with adolescents with intellectual and mental health disabilities, assisting them with identifying and setting attainable goals and supporting them as they worked toward achieving those goals. This included helping adolescents navigate challenges at school and at home, develop greater independence, communicate effectively, and learn strategies for managing difficult situations. I understand the importance of meeting each adolescent at their individual level of development and adapting support to their unique strengths and needs.

Additionally, I have provided home-based support to at-risk adolescents and their families. In this capacity, I worked with both the adolescent and the family system to improve communication, address behavioral and relational challenges, and develop strategies that would allow the family to function more successfully together. A primary goal of this work was to help maintain the adolescent safely within the home and prevent the need for placement in an alternative setting whenever possible.

These experiences have given me a strong understanding of the challenges adolescents and their families can face and the importance of providing consistent, compassionate, and individualized support. I believe strongly in building genuine relationships with young people and creating an environment where they feel seen, heard, respected, and encouraged to recognize their own potential.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, commitment, and passion for working with adolescents to your organization. I am confident that my background in education, mental health, disability services, family support, goal development, and life-skills coaching would allow me to make a meaningful contribution to the adolescents and families you serve.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and background may be a strong fit for your team.

Sincerely,

Debby Silla

candidates.summary:
Throughout my professional career, I have had extensive experience working with adolescents and their families in a variety of settings, with a consistent focus on helping young people develop the skills, confidence, and support necessary to succeed at home, in school, and within their communities.

My experience working with adolescents began as the Director of a therapeutic after-school program serving at-risk middle school children. In this role, I worked closely with adolescents who were experiencing academic, behavioral, social, and family challenges. I provided guidance and support while helping students develop positive coping skills, improve relationships, and recognize their strengths and potential.

I later worked with adolescents with special needs, focusing on goal setting and helping them develop the skills necessary to identify, work toward, and achieve personal goals. I supported adolescents as they navigated challenges in both school and home environments, helping them problem-solve, communicate effectively, and develop greater independence. This experience strengthened my ability to meet adolescents where they were developmentally and to adapt my approach to their individual needs and abilities.

I also worked with at-risk children and their families in a home-based setting. In this role, I provided support not only to the adolescent but to the entire family system. I helped parents and children identify challenges, improve communication, develop healthier patterns of interaction, and establish strategies that would allow the family to function more successfully together. A significant part of this work involved helping families maintain stability so that the adolescent could remain safely and successfully in the home rather than requiring placement in an alternative setting.

Across these experiences, I have developed a strong understanding of the importance of building genuine relationships with adolescents and creating an environment in which they feel heard, respected, and supported. I believe that adolescents are more likely to engage in meaningful change when they are given the opportunity to identify their own strengths, participate in setting their goals, and have consistent adults who believe in their ability to succeed.

My work with adolescents has taught me the importance of patience, active listening, collaboration, and individualized support. Whether working with a young person individually, within a school environment, or alongside their family, my goal has always been to help adolescents develop the skills and confidence they need to navigate challenges and move toward greater independence and success.

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Behavioral Health Recruiter position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. What immediately drew me to AWA is the opportunity to bring together the two sides of my professional career that have always been deeply connected: people and systems. I have spent my career helping organizations find, support, communicate with, and advocate for people—while also building the systems, relationships, and processes that allow people to do their best work.

In my current work with the Washington State Department of Children, Youth, and Families, I bring direct Human Resources experience within a complex public-sector organization serving children, youth, families, and communities. My work requires careful communication, confidentiality, high-volume information triage, policy and procedure navigation, documentation, follow-through, and the ability to recognize when an issue requires additional expertise or escalation. I understand that effective HR is not simply about filling a position—it is about helping the right people find the right environment to do meaningful work.

That perspective is especially valuable in behavioral health.

My broader background includes youth services and juvenile corrections, Agency Affiliated Counselor work, certified victim services advocacy, crisis-line training and supervision, trauma-informed care, de-escalation, domestic violence and abuse recovery services, contract Batterers Intervention work, workforce development, and coaching and consulting support. I have also supported helping professionals and coaching/counseling practices, giving me firsthand appreciation for the communication, emotional intelligence, professionalism, boundaries, and organizational support required in people-centered fields.

I also bring a strong communications foundation developed through more than two decades in media, public communication, interviewing, professional correspondence, and relationship-building. I know how to ask good questions, listen for what is underneath the answer, communicate clearly with different audiences, and represent an organization with professionalism and authenticity. Those skills translate directly into candidate outreach, screening conversations, relationship management, interview coordination, candidate experience, and employer branding.

I would bring AWA a recruiter who understands that behavioral-health professionals are not interchangeable applicants. They are people choosing where to invest their expertise, energy, and compassion. Recruiting them well requires more than matching keywords to a job description. It requires understanding the mission, communicating the opportunity honestly, identifying alignment, creating a respectful candidate experience, and building enough trust that strong professionals want to join the organization.

That is the kind of recruiting I want to do.

I am particularly excited about the opportunity to help AWA grow a team capable of delivering meaningful behavioral-health services to adolescents and their families. My background allows me to understand the clinical and human-services environment while also bringing the HR, workforce, communications, technology, and operational skills necessary to support a growing organization.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring that combination to Adolescent Wellness Academy and help you find the people who can help advance your mission.

Thank you for your consideration. I would be grateful for the opportunity to speak with you.

Sincerely,

Shaylyn Connelly
503-791-8289
Shaylyn.connelly@outlook.com

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in a behavioral health leadership, clinical operations, or clinical management opportunity within your organization. With a PhD in Psychology, Master’s-level training in Psychology, MCAP/CAP credentials, and extensive experience in behavioral health, substance use treatment, clinical supervision, and program operations, I bring a combination of clinical knowledge, leadership experience, and operational expertise that allows me to effectively support both clients and multidisciplinary teams.

I currently serve as a Clinical Director with Recovery Unplugged, where I provide clinical leadership within a substance use and co-occurring mental health treatment environment serving clients across residential and outpatient levels of care. My responsibilities include supporting clinical programming, supervising and collaborating with treatment professionals, reviewing clinical documentation, monitoring treatment progress, addressing client needs, facilitating therapeutic programming, and helping maintain quality and continuity of care. My experience with clinical systems and documentation platforms, including KIPU and other behavioral health technologies, has strengthened my ability to manage clinical operations while maintaining attention to compliance, documentation, and patient-centered care.

Prior to my current role, I developed significant leadership experience within behavioral health and correctional settings, including supervisory responsibilities across multiple facilities and teams. Throughout my career, I have been entrusted with increasing levels of responsibility, progressing from direct-service substance abuse counseling into supervisory and leadership positions. I have experience conducting clinical and operational reviews, supporting staff development, coordinating services, addressing complex client needs, and maintaining program standards. My background has also required me to work effectively with individuals experiencing substance use disorders, mental health concerns, trauma-related challenges, and complex psychosocial circumstances.

My academic and professional background has provided me with a strong foundation in evidence-based behavioral health practices, clinical assessment, treatment planning, group facilitation, and organizational leadership. I approach leadership with a balance of accountability and compassion, recognizing that successful clinical programs depend not only on quality services for clients but also on strong communication, effective supervision, teamwork, and a culture that supports professional growth.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical experience, leadership background, and commitment to behavioral health to your organization. I am confident that my combination of direct clinical experience and executive-level operational perspective would allow me to contribute meaningfully to your team and the individuals you serve.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and qualifications can support your organization’s goals.

Sincerely,

Dr. Richild Morgan, PhD, MCAP
Behavioral Health Executive | Clinical Director | Clinical Operations Leader
Fort Lauderdale–Miami, Florida

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Program Operations Manager position with Adolescent Behavioral Health. With a background in forensic psychology and healthcare operations, combined with several years of experience leading teams, developing workflows, and supporting patients and healthcare partners, I am excited by the opportunity to bring my leadership and operational experience to an organization focused on improving the lives of adolescents and their families.

In my current role within a healthcare organization specializing in Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) and Chronic Care Management (CCM), I lead a team of 13 employees supporting patients, healthcare providers, and clinical partners. I joined the organization while it was still a young startup with limited structure and had the opportunity to help build and develop the support operation as the company grew. This experience has taught me how to thrive in fast-paced environments, identify operational gaps, build practical solutions, and lead teams through change.

My academic background in forensic psychology has given me a strong foundation in behavioral science, human development, and the factors that influence behavior and decision-making. I am particularly drawn to adolescent behavioral health because of the opportunity to combine that academic foundation with my professional experience in healthcare, leadership, and operations. While I am not a clinician, I understand the importance of creating an environment where clinical teams can do their work effectively and where patients and families feel supported, respected, and cared for.

As a leader, I take a hands-on and collaborative approach. I believe in setting clear expectations, supporting employees with the resources and coaching they need to succeed, and holding people accountable while recognizing their strengths and contributions. I also enjoy building structure in evolving environments and continuously looking for ways to improve workflows, communication, and the overall experience for both staff and the individuals we serve.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my healthcare leadership experience, operational mindset, and background in forensic psychology to your team. I am particularly excited about the possibility of contributing to a growing behavioral-health program where strong operations and compassionate leadership can directly support better outcomes for adolescents and their families.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and perspective could contribute to your organization.

Sincerely,
Mariam Dominguez

Why did you leave, or why are you considering leaving, this role?
questionnaire.response: I have gained a tremendous amount of valuable experience in my current role, particularly in leadership, team management, healthcare operations, and process improvement. I am very grateful for the opportunity to grow from an individual contributor into a leadership position and to develop skills that I know will continue to serve me throughout my career.  At this point, however, I am looking for an opportunity to reconnect with the area I am most passionate about: forensic psychology, community work, and helping individuals who may be facing difficult circumstances. My academic background and earlier professional experiences were centered around the forensic and legal systems, and I have always felt strongly that this is the type of work I ultimately want to return to. I would like to use the leadership and operational experience I have gained in healthcare while getting my foot back in the door within a field that is more closely aligned with my education and long-term career goals.  I am also ready to return to an in-person work environment. My current position is entirely remote, and while I have learned a great deal from that experience, I genuinely miss the collaboration, connection, and sense of purpose that comes from working alongside people in person and being directly involved in the community.  Overall, I am not looking to leave my current role because of a negative experience. I am looking for the next step that brings together the leadership skills I have developed with the work I am genuinely passionate about and want to continue building my career around.

questionnaire.text: Who was (or is) your direct supervisor in this role?
questionnaire.body: Please provide their name, title, professional email address, and phone number.

questionnaire.text: If we asked this supervisor about your performance, what would they say was your most significant area for growth, and why?
questionnaire.response: I think my supervisor would say that one of my biggest areas for growth has been learning to delegate more effectively and not feeling like I need to personally take ownership of every problem.  I naturally take a very hands-on approach to my work, and when something needs to be done, my instinct is often to jump in and make sure it gets done correctly. Earlier in my leadership experience, that sometimes meant taking on more than I needed to instead of trusting my team to take ownership themselves.  As I have grown as a manager, I have learned that effective leadership is not about being the person who solves every problem. It is about developing your team, giving people ownership, and knowing when your involvement is most valuable. I have become much more intentional about delegating responsibilities, setting clear expectations, and allowing my team to work through challenges while remaining available to support them.  I still consider myself a very hands-on leader, but I have learned how to balance that with giving my team the autonomy they need to grow. I think that has been an important part of my development as a manager.

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Principles Recovery Center.

client assessments, intake documentation, referrals, and treatment coordination, and a personal
understanding of the recovery journey, I believe I would bring a valuable combination of practical

ability to manage competing priorities, maintain organized documentation, communicate effectively with
clinical professionals, and help individuals identify appropriate next steps in their treatment.

record documentation and digital workflow and information-tracking tools. My experience working

documentation, communication, and follow-through necessary for a successful remote admissions role. I
am comfortable learning new technology and would welcome the opportunity to become proficient in the
specific systems and procedures used by Principles Recovery Center.
Beyond my professional qualifications, my personal recovery journey has given me a deep appreciation
for the courage it takes to ask for help. I understand that individuals seeking treatment for substance use
disorders and co-occurring mental health conditions may feel overwhelmed, uncertain, or hesitant to
take the next step. I believe every person deserves to be met with dignity, patience, and compassion
rather than judgment. I would bring that philosophy to every interaction with prospective clients and their
families, helping them feel heard, understand their options, and navigate the admissions process with
confidence.
I recognize that effective admissions coordination requires both a compassionate approach and
consistent attention to detail. My background in assessments, intake documentation, treatment referrals,
resource research, and coordination with counselors and case managers aligns well with the
responsibilities outlined in your posting. I would be eager to build on this foundation while expanding my
knowledge of PHP and IOP treatment options and contributing to the timely, organized coordination of
admissions.
I am particularly drawn to Principles Recovery Center's people-first approach and its commitment to
helping individuals take their first steps toward recovery. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my
professional experience, independent work style, technical skills, and genuine commitment to supporting

candidates.cover_letter:
I am writing to express my interest in joining your team. With experience spanning higher education, operations, executive support, recruiting, and sustainability, I have built a strong foundation in program coordination, administration, and relationship management. I am excited to contribute my organizational skills, adaptability, and passion for supporting meaningful work.
Growing up in a military family gave me the opportunity to live in many different places and connect with people from diverse backgrounds. These experiences taught me adaptability, strong communication, and the ability to thrive in new environments. I later earned dual bachelor's degrees in Environmental Studies and Fashion Merchandising from Kent State University, where I also competed as a Division I cross-country and track and field student-athlete.
Since graduating in 2020, I have developed a diverse professional background that has strengthened my ability to manage competing priorities, build relationships, and improve operational processes. In my current role as an Outreach Program Officer at Kent State University, I support the NYC Fashion study-away program by coordinating student onboarding and orientation, managing records and data, overseeing facility access, and ensuring smooth day-to-day operations. Working across multiple university departments has strengthened my ability to coordinate complex processes while providing excellent support to students and colleagues.
Previously, I managed teams at Starbucks before transitioning into sustainability-focused work with Spencer Ogden, recruiting professionals into the energy sector. I later joined American Circular Textiles, where I combined research, executive support, and administrative responsibilities while helping advance textile waste policy initiatives. Across these roles, I have managed client communications, coordinated executive travel, supported daily operations, and improved workflows using tools including Excel, Google Workspace, Asana, Slack, Gusto, and ChatGPT.
Throughout my career, I have discovered a passion for building organized, efficient systems that help programs and people succeed. I enjoy creating structure that enables teams to focus on their broader mission, and I am eager to bring my administrative experience, collaborative mindset, and commitment to continuous improvement to a new opportunity.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience and enthusiasm can contribute to your organization. I look forward to hearing from you.

October 13, 2026

Hiring Manager
Principles Recovery Center

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Substance Use Treatment
Dear Hiring Manager,

Throughout my career in behavioral health, I have had the privilege of walking alongside individuals during some of the most difficult and vulnerable moments of their lives. I have witnessed firsthand the challenges of addiction, the courage it takes to ask for help, and the incredible difference that access to appropriate treatment can make. These experiences have not only shaped me as a professional but have strengthened my belief that everyone deserves to feel supported, understood, and hopeful when taking their first steps toward recovery. It is with this passion that I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Principles Recovery Center.

In my current role as a behavioral health counselor, I work extensively with individuals experiencing substance use disorders and co-occurring mental health challenges. My responsibilities include conducting comprehensive assessments, determining appropriate levels of care using ASAM criteria, developing individualized treatment recommendations, and helping coordinate referrals to additional treatment services. Through my work with Intensive Outpatient Programs, outpatient services, and residential treatment referrals, I have developed a strong understanding of the treatment continuum and the importance of helping individuals access care that meets their unique needs.

One of the most meaningful aspects of my work has been building connections with individuals who may feel overwhelmed, discouraged, or uncertain about seeking treatment. I understand that reaching out for help is not always easy and that the compassion, patience, and understanding someone receives during those initial interactions can make a lasting difference. I strive to approach every individual with dignity, empathy, and encouragement while helping them navigate the often-complex process of accessing behavioral health services.

In addition to my clinical experience, I bring strong organizational, communication, and care coordination skills. Managing a substantial caseload has strengthened my ability to balance competing priorities, maintain accurate documentation, communicate effectively with multidisciplinary providers, and ensure that individuals receive appropriate follow-up and support. I am comfortable working independently, navigating electronic health records, and collaborating with community partners to reduce barriers to treatment.

What excites me most about this opportunity is the ability to continue making a meaningful difference in the lives of individuals seeking recovery while focusing my professional skills on connecting people with the services they need. I believe the admissions process is much more than an administrative responsibility; it is an opportunity to offer reassurance, build trust, and help someone recognize that recovery is possible.

I would be honored to bring my experience, dedication, and genuine compassion for individuals in recovery to the admissions team at Principles Recovery Center. Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my background and passion for helping others could contribute to your organization's mission.
Sincerely,

Cynthia “Morgan” Fazekas
